content:
Siri AI is a major upgrade to Apple's assistant, expected to launch with iOS 27. I've noticed one significant difference from other AI assistants, and it's a good one.

The new Siri on iOS 27 won't pretend to be human, setting it completely apart from other AI chatbots

I've been using the Siri AI on the iOS 27 beta for nearly two months. So far, it has done everything I hoped it would.

The new Siri is far more capable than its predecessor, finally delivering on Apple's original promise of a truly capable assistant on its devices.

However, I do acknowledge that if you need the absolute cutting-edge, most powerful AI tools out there, competitors like ChatGPT, Claude, and Google Gemini may be better suited for you.

That said, after using Siri AI and comparing it with these third-party tools, I discovered one key difference that makes me lean heavily toward Siri.

Unlike other AI chatbots, Siri doesn't pretend to be human.

It doesn't go on at excessive length or mimic human-like personalities to build a personal relationship with you.

Siri is helpful, smart, and does what you ask. But the way it responds makes clear that it's a tool, not a person. It periodically reminds you that it's an AI and may make mistakes. It also won't pretend to go on a date with you.

On the other hand, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini are all full of personality and opinions, showing more human-like tendencies—which I find disingenuous.

I suppose some users prefer that more "personal" approach. But I much prefer an AI assistant that stays in its lane and doesn't put on an act.

AI is changing the world. But AI chatbots are tools, not people. I'm glad Apple understands this and has built the new Siri accordingly.

What do you think about how "human-like" AI assistants should be? Share your views in the comments section.
